questions.implements: Does the diff implement what the user asked for, and add or change a test that checks it? Judge the code in the diff, not the answer.

judge.reason: The diff does what R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT asks. `Cart.VolumeDiscount` takes 5% off each line with 10 or more units, and integer division rounds each line down to the cent on its own. `PriceWithVolume` subtracts the volume discount first and applies the discount code to what is left. It then caps the combined discount at MaxDiscountPercent (the 50% cap) of the original subtotal. `PlaceOrder` now uses this path, so the change reaches checkout. Three new tests check it. `TestVolumeDiscount` covers the 10-unit threshold and per-line rounding down (10.50 becomes 10 cents and 6.05 becomes 6, for 16 cents total). `TestPriceWithVolume` checks that the volume discount comes before the code and that the cap holds when the combined discount would pass 50%. `TestPlaceOrderVolumeDiscount` checks the full checkout flow. The expected numbers in all three match the rule when worked out by hand.

finalMessage:
Implemented SHOP-57 (`R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT`). Cart lines with at least 10 units now receive 5% off, rounded down per line. Checkout applies a discount code afterward and caps the combined discount at 50% of the original subtotal.

`go test ./...` passes. `ostf check --base main` reports 115 valid links and no errors. The impact includes `R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT`, `R-CHECKOUT-ORDER`, `R-CHECKOUT-SESSION`, and `R-TAX-RATE`; its listed tests are `TestVolumeDiscount`, `TestPlaceOrder`, `TestPlaceOrderNeedsSession`, `TestPlaceOrderVolumeDiscount`, `TestPrice`, `TestPriceWithVolume`, and `TestTax`. Six links were added for `R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT`: implementation links to `Cart.VolumeDiscount`, `PriceWithVolume`, and `Checkout.PlaceOrder`, and verification links to the three new tests.
